summary: The LLM landscape in late 2026 is dominated by OpenAI's GPT family, which still commands the majority of consumer AI traffic and developer API volume, though its share has eroded as Google Gemini, Anthropic Claude, and open-weight challengers like Meta Llama, DeepSeek, and Alibaba Qwen gain ground. Enterprise adoption increasingly flows through cloud aggregators (AWS Bedrock, Azure OpenAI, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, IBM watsonx), which meaningfully amplifies real-world reach for models available across multiple platforms. Open-weight models have become central to developer workflows via HuggingFace downloads and self-hosting, clustering tightly in adoption behind the proprietary leaders.

models.name: GPT-5
models.popularity_notes: ChatGPT accounted for 55.5% of worldwide generative AI website visits (532B web visits) and OpenAI leads developer API volume, with availability through Azure OpenAI Service extending enterprise reach.
models.best_for: General-purpose applications requiring top-tier reasoning and broad integration support

models.name: Gemini 3 Pro
models.popularity_notes: Google Gemini ranked second with 1.14 billion visits and 26.9% chatbot market share, with deep enterprise distribution via Google Vertex AI.
strengths: Tight Google Cloud and Workspace integration
models.best_for: Long-context and multimodal enterprise workloads within the Google ecosystem

models.name: Claude Opus 4.5
models.popularity_notes: Claude ranked third with 968 million visits and is a developer favorite for coding, with enterprise availability across AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex.
models.best_for: Agentic coding assistants and enterprise workflows prioritizing reliability

models.name: Llama 4
models.popularity_notes: Meta's Llama remains the most downloaded open-weight family on HuggingFace and is available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx, giving it unmatched aggregator reach among open models.
strengths: Open weights for self-hosting and fine-tuning
models.best_for: Self-hosted and customizable enterprise deployments requiring open weights

models.name: GPT-5 mini
models.popularity_notes: The cost-efficient GPT-5 tier drives very high API call volume for production workloads where cost matters, amplified by Azure OpenAI availability.
strengths: Strong general capability for its tier
models.best_for: High-throughput production applications needing a balance of cost and quality

models.name: DeepSeek-V3.2
models.popularity_notes: DeepSeek was the highest-ranked Chinese AI tool with 319 million visits and its open-weight models see heavy HuggingFace downloads due to very low cost.
models.best_for: Cost-sensitive reasoning and coding tasks with optional self-hosting

models.name: Gemini 3 Flash
models.popularity_notes: The Flash tier is a high-volume workhorse for latency-sensitive applications, widely consumed via Google Vertex AI in enterprise pipelines.
models.best_for: High-volume, low-latency multimodal applications at scale

models.name: Qwen3
models.popularity_notes: Qwen is among the most downloaded open-weight families on HuggingFace and is cited as a top-9 LLM, with growing availability through cloud platforms.
models.best_for: Multilingual and self-hosted deployments needing flexible model sizing

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.popularity_notes: The fast, affordable Claude tier sees heavy production API usage and shares Claude's broad aggregator reach across Bedrock, Vertex AI, and Snowflake Cortex.
strengths: Strong tool use for its tier
models.best_for: Latency-sensitive agentic and chat applications at lower cost

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.popularity_notes: Mistral's models have strong European enterprise adoption and are available across AWS Bedrock, Azure, Google Vertex AI, Snowflake Cortex, and IBM watsonx, with open-weight variants popular on HuggingFace.
models.best_for: European and privacy-conscious enterprise deployments with aggregator access
